answer.rationale: Only the low-cost vendor's quote clears the 18% mandate on its own, and the incumbent has already refused to reopen price, which directly contradicts the precondition behind memory_c4 (benchmarking moved them) and rules out negotiate_terms as a standalone answer this cycle. memory_c6's volume-discount path also depends on the incumbent being willing to price, so it is not live. defer_decision is unsafe here in a way memory_c5 does not cover: that memory concerned a non-critical, month-to-month service, whereas this contract expires in 14 days and does not auto-renew, so deferral means an actual supply gap at 94% committed volume with no buffer. memory_c3 (dual sourcing held allocation through a shortage) is the most attractive risk posture, but adding a second source does not by itself resolve the expiring primary contract and would likely miss the cost mandate. So the intent is to move primary supply to the low-cost vendor, which is why memory_c2 is the single load-bearing claim and the one I spend the verification pull on. What I need from the archive is exactly what memory_c2 does not say: it attests to unit cost, onboarding speed, and invoicing accuracy, but nothing about sustained on-time delivery at full committed volume, and it is dated 'last year' with a day-38 consolidation, so the underlying record may reflect a smaller order book or a different capacity picture. If the source shows the prior award was a partial or low-volume tranche, the cost claim does not transfer to a full-line switch. Consequently I scope this as a staged cutover rather than a clean flip: qualify the vendor on a bounded share of committed volume with a short incumbent bridge on the remainder and hard on-time and defect gates before full transfer, so the 94% utilization with zero buffer is not exposed to an unproven ramp. Downstream risk is real and flagged: a cost-only optimization can quietly convert into delivery failure, and per-unit savings validated at low volume can reverse once expedite and shortfall costs land in total cost of ownership. I am not treating memory_c2 as settled proof of vendor capacity; if the archived record is silent on volume performance, the correct fallback is a bridge extension plus dual sourcing in the next review rather than a full switch.
